memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Joseph saw his father placing his right hand on Ephraim's head he was displeased; so he took hold of his father's hand to move it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's head. Joseph said to him, 'No, my father, this one is the firstborn; put your right hand on his head.'" — Gen 48:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph is displeased, and he does something quite remarkable — he physically takes hold of his father's hand to move it.

He is not being wicked. He genuinely believes his father has made a mistake. The old man is blind; perhaps he has simply got confused about which boy is which. Joseph is trying to correct an error.

But there is no error. Joseph is trying to move God's hand back into the position he thinks it belongs.

We do this constantly. We have a clear idea of how God ought to arrange things — who should be blessed, which door should open, how the situation should resolve — and when His hand lands somewhere unexpected, our instinct is to correct Him.

Peter did exactly this when Jesus spoke of the cross: "Never, Lord! This shall never happen to you!" (Matt 16:22). He was sincere, and he was completely wrong. What looked like a disaster to him was the salvation of the world.

Be slow to assume God has made a mistake. The times His hand lands somewhere strange are usually the times He is doing something we cannot yet see.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you tried to move God's hand to where you thought it belonged?
2. Has something you resisted turned out to be God's better plan?
3. How do you respond when God's arrangement does not match your expectation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for the times I have tried to correct You. Give me the humility to trust Your hand where it lands, even when I do not understand it. Amen.
